The project extended far beyond a single film.
The visual system was prepared for multiple applications, including digital media and the launch presentation at Interpack 2026, where the Brand Movie became part of a large-scale ultra-wide LED installation featuring different playback scenarios for the individual performance brands and the GroupMosca presentation.
Aixsponza assembled the final exhibition version, produced the high-resolution masters and coordinated the technical implementation across the complete playback environment.

caption_text:
Turning creative direction into a coherent brand experience.
Created for the launch of GroupMosca, the Brand Movie introduces the company's evolution towards an integrated End-of-Line ecosystem and its vision of transforming supply chains into intelligent lifelines.
Developed by klee.steinberger, the new brand identity established the strategic and visual foundation for the project. Building on this direction, designer Maido Hollo developed the abstract visual language and directed the cinematic opening sequence that introduces the GroupMosca universe.
Working as Creative Production Partner, Aixsponza collaborated throughout the evolving production process, contributing to the creative development while taking responsibility for translating an evolving creative concept into a production that remained visually consistent across multiple contributors, formats and delivery platforms.

caption_text:
Checker Tobi 3 / The Secret Ruler of Earth
We had the pleasure of creating the animated explainer sequences for Checker Tobi 1 and Checker Tobi 2 and now we are very happy to continue the journey with Checker Tobi 3.
Once again, the film blends children’s education with curiosity and fun, brought to life through playful claydough inspired stop motion visuals. These explainers are always a highlight for us because they have a clear purpose, tell meaningful stories, and are made for the big screen.
A big thank you to @megaherz.film for trusting us yet again with these sequences. It is a joy to be part of a project that sparks curiosity and makes learning feel like an adventure.
Find the full project overview at aixsponza.com

In 1902 the Venice Campanile collapsed. In 1911 Denver built a taller copy - and the papers joked Venice was copying Denver.
Murano//HUD:$ync.DF returns the glass to the ghost: Simulated Venetian glass on a Venetian tower that outlived its own original, now displaying time it never kept.

A clock tower that wears time instead of telling it.
For one month, Denver's Daniels & Fisher Tower was dressed in Venetian glass. The surface twitches once per second- seconds passing, rendered as glass instead of digits. And the host is perfect, as it is also a simulation: the tower is a 1911 replica of the Campanile di San Marco in Venice. We reconnected it back to Venice with a simulation of its Murano Glass.

caption_text:
Avito came to us with a challenge: to move beyond its long-standing image as a digital flea market. The brand had outgrown its cheerful, chaotic visual language, and needed a design system that felt just as friendly — but more professional and dynamic.
We introduced a couple of solutions, one of which was the Graphic Collider — a visual framework built on the idea of motion, depth, and interaction. Its radial energy reflects Avito’s core: a place where countless goods and services connect and accelerate.
As part of the redesign, we also developed widgets — a new layer of visual communication that blends 3D objects with interface elements, showing how the platform works in a more tangible and engaging way.

As part of the redesign, we also developed widgets — a new layer of visual communication that blends 3D objects with interface elements, showing how the platform works in a more tangible and engaging way.

caption_text:
User interface design for Black Adam.
Given that my background is half Egyptian, I was super excited to weave in the Eye of Horus—a powerful symbol in ancient Egyptian culture representing protection, health, and restoration—as the main structure of this operating system.
As you can see in the last image, we used the set design of the tapered glass shape as inspiration for our eye outline. Within this, we created an OS with data streams flowing along the Horus pathways.
In the same image, just to the left of the crown, is the central operating interface. It functions as the hub, contextually positioning and distributing information to the rest of the operating system.
Another great one working with Cantina Creative, visual effects supervisor Aaron Eaton, and visual effects producer Sean Cushing.‌
Also, I’m putting together a course — my process, my decisions, the craft, everything I’ve learned from over 10 years of making art for films.
I’m doing early access pricing for a while if you’re interested → Link in bio!

caption_text:
Designing UI for Top Gun: Maverick.
Being a part of movies is something really special to me. It is design, but it’s also art.
Connecting to the art and expression is so important to me. We’re designers, but we’re also artists.
Doing art, and being a part of an art piece goes beyond design, practicality, AI presence, logic, etc. It’s ultimately about what makes us feel excited, truly.
This is what I’m trying to cultivate for myself every day. Remembering to sink into feeling and exploration because that is what can fuel us.
What’s making you excited lately? Please DM me some recommendations!
Always love to hear from you all. It always opens up my world when we chat.
Also, thank you for all the early pricing signups for my Film UI design course! It’s been so nice to see the feedback. If you’re interested, early access pricing link is in my bio.

caption_text:
The Top Gun: Maverick Tactical Flag Command Center.
I rewatched Top Gun: Maverick in theaters last weekend and then came home and dug through all the work I did for it and found these — the Tactical Flag Command Center.
These went through a lot of color iteration, but I always loved this look and feel. It’s such a fun challenge to try to create this stuff quickly while still giving it special meaning and care. I haven’t looked at these in depth for a while, so it’s been fun to reconnect to the energy and thoughts I had working on this film.
I’m very happy I chose to express art and design in this way as my path.
I’m putting together a course on how this work actually gets made — my process, my decisions, the craft, everything I’ve learned from over 10 years of making art for films.
If you want in at early access pricing, drop your email here → link in bio
🖤

caption_text:
This post isn’t for everyone.
One of the first films I worked on was The Fate of the Furious.
Cantina Creative and Sean Cushing gave me a chance to join them when I had no credits and barely any portfolio.
They were my favorite design studio.
When I arrived, I got to meet and work with one of my design heroes, Alan Torres.
He helped me tremendously in every way.
I always share this story with people who ask me for advice—he positioned me in ways I can’t even begin to quantify. When someone is that good, unique, kind, and supportive, it changes everything.
I’m very thankful for all the luck I’ve had, but I do broadly believe in what baseball legend Branch Rickey famously remarked: “Luck is the residue of design.”
That’s why I try to mentor as many people as I can, to help them build their own “design.”
People helped me, and we should do the same if we have something to offer.
So today, I’m grateful for my luck. And if I can offer anything in the way of career and design advice, it’s this—reach out to people and talk to them. We can help each other.
As of late, my inbox has been filled more and more with people worried about the state of the world and art with regards to AI, and so now more than ever we need to talk to each other.
It’s helped me tremendously, and I try to pass that help on every day. So, as many of you know, my inbox is open.
As always, I’ll do my best to help. 🖤

caption_text:
Pedrera with structured glass tops by Spanish architect Barba Corsini.
The Pedrera coffee table is reimagined with three textured glass tops that bring color and sensory depth to Spanish architect Barba Corsini’s beloved first design of Pedrera in 1955. The new structured glass tops come in transparent, smoke, and bronze.
Inspired by the rippling play of water and the undulating contours of La Pedrera, the structured glass surfaces enrich corsini’s well-loved silhouette with a fresh material identity.
The products are real and based on photographs. The direction, art direction and styling was done by the team at Frame. The renderings and animations were produced utilizing AI.

The Pedrera coffee table is reimagined with three textured glass tops that bring color and sensory depth to Spanish architect Barba Corsini’s beloved first design of Pedrera in 1955. The new structured glass tops come in transparent, smoke, and bronze.
Inspired by the rippling play of water and the undulating contours of La Pedrera, the structured glass surfaces enrich corsini’s well-loved silhouette with a fresh material identity.
The products are real and based on photographs. The direction, art direction and styling was done by the team at Frame. The renderings and stills were produced utilizing AI.

caption_text:
Waves, developed by Kvadrat Acoustics in collaboration with Foster + Partners Industrial Design, is a new acoustic curtain solution designed to create adaptable acoustic soft rooms within open-plan interiors. The system rethinks the curtain as a flexible architectural element – capable of shaping interiors, improving acoustic comfort, and responding to changing user needs.
The film by Frame is designed to highlight the highly adaptable nature of Waves as the product integrates seamlessly with existing architectural structures. It can be installed directly to ceilings, soffits, and beams and is available in both manual and motorised configurations, including app-based control. By softly defining pockets of space within larger environments, the system supports a wide range of activities – from focused work meetings to informal gatherings.

PACHA LOUNGE CHAIR BY PIERRE PAULIN
In his earliest sketches, Pierre Paulin imagined sitting as a sensation, expressed through rounded forms that seem to float and hold the body with ease. From this idea came a new way of sitting: low, generous, and free from convention.
Set within an alpine dreamscape, clouds circle gently, echoing the curves of Pacha. The form drifts between inside and out, lightly touching the ground. Its sculptural volumes feel naturally shaped by time.
The products are real and based on photographs. The direction, art direction, styling and sound design was done by the team at Frame. The renderings, animations and music were produced utilizing AI.

caption_text:
New work for Montblanc.
This time for the Minerva Unveiled Crownless - a stainless steel and rose gold time-only watch that possesses an especially strong symmetry due to its lack of a traditional crown.
The crownless design relies on assigning manual winding and time setting to the fluted bezel, a modern-day innovation inspired by a 1927 Minerva pilot’s watch with a rotating timing bezel. The vintage-shaped stainless steel case is adorned with a rose gold (18 karat) fluted bezel and an inscription “Depuis 1858” on the mid-case.

caption: portablelamp
caption_text:
Wire Ø18 Portable Lamp
VERPAN, design by Verner Panton
We’re pleased to share our first film built entirely with AI, created for VERPAN’s launch of a design classic: the Wire Portable Lamp. At FRAME, we’ve spent 20 years shaping 3D product narratives for leading luxury brands.
This project marks a quiet but important shift. For the first time, AI was the main tool for the entire production. This isn’t a proof of concept. It’s a finished piece for a heritage brand, showcasing a design that’s been around since 1972. The kind of work that demands precise product fidelity and photorealism.
Panton’s Wire Lamp was created in 1972 through a spirit of experimentation. It feels fitting that its newest chapter is brought to life by a tool that encourages exploration once again. AI doesn’t follow a neat, predictable path. It offers a broad landscape of possibilities. Some useful, some unexpected, and a lot downright useless.
Working with it, requires clarity, direction, and a steady hand. When guided professionally, it’s faster, more cost-efficient, and in some ways more creative, without compromising craft. By directing AI deliberately through each stage - ideation, product creation, photorealistic sets, photographic effects, animation, music - we created a film worthy of Panton’s timeless work.
The products are real and based on photographs. The direction, art direction, styling and sound design was done by the team at Frame. The renderings, animations and music were produced utilizing AI.
Thanks for the feature @stashmedia.tv @visualatelier8
@vernerpantonofficial @verpancom #portablelamp

caption_text:
FRAME was thrilled to team up with Danish design house GUBI and create a film to coincide with the release of its new Elogio Sofa. Expressing an inviting softness with architectural structure, the Elogio Sofa is one of the iconic furniture designs to emerge from the husband-and-wife studio of Tobia and Afra Scarpa. Created in 1974 as an evolution of the Erasmo sofa, it introduced a new modular approach to domestic living, allowing for multiple configurations depending on the shape, scale, and style of the space.
Revisited by Tobia Scarpa with GUBI five decades later, this edition has been subtly upgraded to enhance comfort and finesse the geometry of the design. Its interchangeable cushions can be reoriented to suit different needs and upholstery options, including GUBI’s new Reales and Fustagno fabrics, enhance the sofa’s tactile and visual character.
Taking its name from the Italian word for ‘praise’ or ‘tribute’, Elogio celebrates the everyday beauty of domestic life. The system comprises three elements: two modules with side panels and one armless center module. These can be used alone or combined into a wide range of configurations: linear setups, corner compositions, chaise longues, or more experimental arrangements. This versatility makes Elogio ideal for interiors of any size – from compact apartments to expansive open-plan homes and hospitality settings.
Thanks to @visualatelier8 for the feature.

caption_text:
FRAME was thrilled to team up with Danish design house GUBI and create a film to coincide with the release of its new Elogio Sofa. Expressing an inviting softness with architectural structure, the Elogio Sofa is one of the iconic furniture designs to emerge from the husband-and-wife studio of Tobia and Afra Scarpa. Created in 1974 as an evolution of the Erasmo sofa, it introduced a new modular approach to domestic living, allowing for multiple configurations depending on the shape, scale, and style of the space.
Revisited by Tobia Scarpa with GUBI five decades later, this edition has been subtly upgraded to enhance comfort and finesse the geometry of the design. Its interchangeable cushions can be reoriented to suit different needs and upholstery options, including GUBI’s new Reales and Fustagno fabrics, enhance the sofa’s tactile and visual character.
Taking its name from the Italian word for ‘praise’ or ‘tribute’, Elogio celebrates the everyday beauty of domestic life. The system comprises three elements: two modules with side panels and one armless center module. These can be used alone or combined into a wide range of configurations: linear setups, corner compositions, chaise longues, or more experimental arrangements. This versatility makes Elogio ideal for interiors of any size – from compact apartments to expansive open-plan homes and hospitality settings.

caption_text:
Building on a legacy of crafting exquisite instruments that inspire writing, Montblanc brings its storied name to digital writing. Elegantly designed, the Digital Paper and Digital Pen work hand-in-hand to bring your words to life wherever creativity finds you. A selection of interchangeable pen nibs deliver digital ink flow as unique as your own handwriting. Montblanc Digital Paper ensures every note is carefully organised, securely stored, and always within reach.
Inspired by the Montblanc icon, the Digital Pen reflects over a century of writing excellence – reimagined for the connected age. Its sleek silhouette and perfectly weighted body offer lasting comfort for extended writing. Easily accessible buttons allow intuitive control of features, enhancing the user’s flow without distraction.
Modeled on the ergonomic design of the Meisterstück, the Digital Pen features a tool switch and a top button, to enable instant and easy access to all its features. Traditional design cues are echoed on the cap and cone, including the Montblanc emblem and the three engraved metal rings surrounding the Montblanc wordmark.
The signature Montblanc writing experience is brought to life with a digital ink flow through three distinct nibs: Linen, Matte, and Smooth. Each nib emulates a different paper texture, and has been carefully crafted to offer a writing experience tailored to your preference.
Crafted with a sleek metal frame and a high resolution paper-like canvas, the Montblanc Digital Paper stands out as a design piece in its own right. The elegant leather side bar adds a warm, tactile contrast, enhanced by the iconic Montblanc emblem.
Discover endless creativity in a digital notebook that captures the true feel of paper, with room for an entire library of your ideas.

caption_text:
To commemorate its 160th year as one of the world’s leading watchmakers, Zenith teamed up with Frame to create a series of short films highlighting an extremely limited edition release of its three hero products.
The iconic Pilot, Defy and Chronomaster Sport have each been reissued in a cool Zenith blue monochrome edition to mark 160 years of the brand.  Strictly limited to 160 pieces, these unique timepieces have been crafted in ceramic to provide a stunning finish that also underlines Zenith’s commitment to mastering the most complicated of materials.
In addition, the brand used the campaign as an opportunity to reintroduce its core collection to the world, featuring the Pilot, Defy and Chronomaster Sport in their original materials and colourways.  Reminding the world of why the brand has been synonymous with the future of Swiss watchmaking since 1865.
